business_archetype.label: Integrated Delivery Network and Health Plan modernizing toward governed, AI-ready analytics
business_archetype.narrative: Meridian Health System runs both sides of the healthcare economic equation: it delivers care through hospitals and ambulatory clinics and it bears risk as a health plan across claims, pharmacy, utilization management, and member service. This dual model is the strategic advantage and the strategic complexity. Value is created where clinical and claims data meet — population health, cost of care, provider performance, payment integrity — yet those are exactly the places where the evidence base shows the data is not yet unified, governed, or trusted. Meridian is not thin on technology; Epic anchors clinical operations and a substantial claims, pharmacy, CRM, and analytics estate is in production. The gap is not systems — it is a governed foundation that lets those systems answer enterprise questions with confidence.
business_archetype.client_context_signal: Enterprise profile confirms integrated delivery network and health plan archetype with clinical delivery, payer operations, finance, and analytics modernization scope.

governing_thesis.statement: Meridian's leadership has already agreed on the seven business outcomes that matter — a unified clinical and claims view, governed AI, lower call-center cost, stronger provider performance, cost transparency, payment integrity, and faster close. What it has not yet done is build the governed data foundation those outcomes depend on. The executive decision is therefore not which use case to chase, but whether to fund the foundation — medallion architecture, data governance operating model, semantic layer, and member identity spine — as the enterprise's first investment, before treating any individual use case as ready to scale.
governing_thesis.supporting_logic: Seven use cases are source-backed and executive-sponsored across CEO, CFO, CDAO, CMO, and Health Plan Ops interviews. Every use case is gated by the same four cross-cutting foundation gaps: no certified medallion architecture, no formal data governance, no certified semantic layer, and no member identity spine. Two use cases — the lakehouse and governed AI foundation — are prerequisites for the rest.
governing_thesis.so_what_for_leadership: Funding scattered across use cases will stall, because they share the same unbuilt foundation. Sequencing the foundation first converts a stalled portfolio into an executable one.
governing_thesis.client_context_signal: Existing home narrative and evidence-gap summary confirm four high-severity foundation gaps block all seven use cases simultaneously.

chapter_context.title: Where the Industry Is Moving — and What It Means for a Dual Delivery-and-Plan Operator
chapter_context.framing: Meridian competes as both a care provider and a risk-bearing plan. The industry movements that matter most are the ones that reward organizations able to join clinical and claims evidence under governance — exactly the capability Meridian has decided to pursue but not yet built. External momentum therefore raises both the reward for moving and the cost of waiting.

industry_movements.movement: Integrated delivery networks with plan operations are collapsing separate clinical, claims, and pharmacy reporting into one governed foundation so population health, margin, and provider performance answer from the same numbers. The differentiator is no longer holding both datasets — it is trusting a joined view of them.

industry_movements.title: Governed AI is becoming an audit requirement, not an experiment

Healthcare organizations are pausing use cases that cannot evidence governance rather than risk regulatory and clinical exposure.

evidence_maturity_read.headline: The demand signal is well-evidenced; the delivery foundation is not yet certified.
evidence_maturity_read.narrative: Meridian's evidence base is unusually strong on the question of what leadership wants and why it stalls, and deliberately silent on the question of whether the foundation to deliver it exists. Executive interviews across the C-suite, a structured risks-and-controls review, and a validated view of the production system and platform estate together establish, to decision-grade confidence, that seven priority outcomes are sponsored and that all of them converge on the same four unbuilt foundations. That convergence is the most important thing the evidence proves. What the evidence does not prove — and must not be read to imply — is that any governed medallion architecture, unified patient/member view, certified semantic layer, or ready target platform is in place. Every value hypothesis therefore remains a hypothesis: credible enough to fund a foundation program against, not yet measured enough to book.
evidence_maturity_read.read_for_leadership: Treat the portfolio as decision-ready to sequence and fund at the foundation level, and as validation-pending at the individual value-claim level. The gating condition is uniform, which is what makes a single foundation program the highest-leverage move.

client_visible.reason: The pack is business-first, well-classified, and disciplined on value claims, but a small number of structural issues in the relationships section break the closed schema contract and must be corrected before human review. Each graph_projection nests its relationship_graph inside a field named graph_display_contract, which the schema explicitly disallows; the projection object itself must carry the relationship_graph fields directly. In addition, one dimension writer used a heatmap primary_visual with categorical string cell values rather than the compact numeric intensity the renderer expects, and the batch-2 priority_matrix_visual places non-workflow enabler nodes on a use-case priority axis. These are correctable content-contract issues rather than any concern with the underlying analysis, which is coherent across sections.

violations.issue: Each of the six projections nests its relationship_graph visual inside a field named graph_display_contract. The contract states there is no separate graph_display_contract field; a relationship_graph visual object must carry visual_type, projection_type, classification, node_groups, edge_meaning, layout_hint, visual_emphasis, and empty_state directly on the visual object itself.
violations.remediation: Lift the relationship_graph fields onto the projection's own visual object and remove the graph_display_contract wrapper across all six projections.

violations.issue: The apps heatmap uses categorical string cell values (critical, not ready, fragmented, aspirational, high) instead of a compact numeric intensity scale. The renderer expects heatmap color to encode a bounded numeric intensity so the executive can read concentration; mixed string values across two different semantic axes (criticality vs readiness) in one color channel is ambiguous.
violations.remediation: Convert cell values to a single numeric intensity (e.g., 1-3) with a stated color_meaning, keeping criticality and readiness as distinct rows or a clearly-labeled two-column encoding.

violations.issue: Three of four plotted points (Transcript Governance, Member Identity Linkage, Intent Taxonomy) are foundation enablers, not bounded workflows, yet they are placed on an executive-priority-vs-readiness use-case matrix. This risks reading enablers as competing use-case candidates, blurring the foundation/use-case distinction the pack otherwise enforces well.
violations.remediation: Either restrict the matrix to the single workflow candidate with enablers shown as an annotation, or relabel the series/axis so enablers are visibly distinct from the qualified workflow.

violations.issue: module_implications is authored as an object with a headline and implications array here, while in the apps and rel dimensions it is an array of classified implication objects. The inconsistent shape, and the fact that the risks implications strings do not each carry a classification, weakens cross-dimension consistency.
violations.remediation: Align module_implications to the array-of-classified-objects shape used by the apps and rel dimensions, with each implication carrying a single classification.

Labeling directional proxy scores as a derived_measure slightly overstates evidence posture.

business_archetype.label: Integrated Delivery Network and Health Plan modernizing toward governed, AI-ready analytics
business_archetype.narrative: Meridian Health System runs both sides of the healthcare economic equation: it delivers care through hospitals and ambulatory clinics and it bears risk as a health plan across claims, pharmacy, utilization management, and member service. This dual model is the strategic advantage and the strategic complexity. Value is created where clinical and claims data meet — population health, cost of care, provider performance, payment integrity — yet those are exactly the places where the evidence base shows the data is not yet unified, governed, or trusted. Meridian is not thin on technology; Epic anchors clinical operations and a substantial claims, pharmacy, CRM, and analytics estate is in production. The gap is not systems — it is a governed foundation that lets those systems answer enterprise questions with confidence.
business_archetype.client_context_signal: Enterprise profile confirms integrated delivery network and health plan archetype with clinical delivery, payer operations, finance, and analytics modernization scope.

governing_thesis.statement: Meridian's leadership has already agreed on the seven business outcomes that matter — a unified clinical and claims view, governed AI, lower call-center cost, stronger provider performance, cost transparency, payment integrity, and faster close. What it has not yet done is build the governed data foundation those outcomes depend on. The executive decision is therefore not which use case to chase, but whether to fund the foundation — medallion architecture, data governance operating model, semantic layer, and member identity spine — as the enterprise's first investment, before treating any individual use case as ready to scale.
governing_thesis.supporting_logic: Seven use cases are source-backed and executive-sponsored across CEO, CFO, CDAO, CMO, and Health Plan Ops interviews. Every use case is gated by the same four cross-cutting foundation gaps: no certified medallion architecture, no formal data governance, no certified semantic layer, and no member identity spine. Two use cases — the lakehouse and governed AI foundation — are prerequisites for the rest.
governing_thesis.so_what_for_leadership: Funding scattered across use cases will stall, because they share the same unbuilt foundation. Sequencing the foundation first converts a stalled portfolio into an executable one.

chapter_context.title: Where the Industry Is Moving — and What It Means for a Dual Delivery-and-Plan Operator
chapter_context.framing: Meridian competes as both a care provider and a risk-bearing plan. The industry movements that matter most are the ones that reward organizations able to join clinical and claims evidence under governance — exactly the capability Meridian has decided to pursue but not yet built. External momentum therefore raises both the reward for moving and the cost of waiting.

industry_movements.movement: Integrated delivery networks with plan operations are collapsing separate clinical, claims, and pharmacy reporting into one governed foundation so population health, margin, and provider performance answer from the same numbers. use_cases.section_title: Use-Case Qualification — Batch 1 of the Seven Agreed Outcomes

executive_framing.message: These four candidates sort into two categories leadership must treat differently. The lakehouse and the AI/LLM governance base are not use cases at all — they are the shared foundation that every other outcome depends on, and they should be funded first as one program. Payment integrity and cost transparency are genuine bounded workflows with real value at stake, but neither is decision-grade today: both draw on claims and contract data already in Meridian's estate yet remain blocked by the same unbuilt governance, semantic, and identity foundation. The disciplined move is to fund the foundation, then release these two workflows against signed-off baselines — not to chase them individually on an unbuilt base.

summary_tab.headline: The systems are not the problem — the absence of a governed layer connecting them is
summary_tab.executive_read: Meridian runs a mature, mission-critical application estate: Epic anchors clinical operations, dedicated platforms carry claims and pharmacy, and finance, CRM, contact-center, and multiple analytics environments are all in production. This is an asset to leverage, not a greenfield to invent. The constraint is that these systems operate as vertical strengths with no governed layer above them — clinical, claims, contract, and financial data are not harmonized, identity is not resolved across them, and reporting logic is duplicated across separate BI environments. As a result, every priority outcome that depends on combining these systems remains blocked at the same point. AWS and Databricks are the stated destination for that governed layer but are directional, not certified. Leadership should treat this estate as proven operational infrastructure whose enterprise value is locked until a governed foundation sits on top of it.

violations.issue: The apps heatmap uses categorical string cell values (critical, not ready, fragmented, aspirational, high) instead of a compact numeric intensity scale. The renderer expects heatmap color to encode a bounded numeric intensity so the executive can read concentration; mixed string values across two different semantic axes (criticality vs readiness) in one color channel is ambiguous.
violations.remediation: Convert cell values to a single numeric intensity (e.g., 1-3) with a stated color_meaning, keeping criticality and readiness as distinct rows or a clearly-labeled two-column encoding.

violations.issue: Three of four plotted points (Transcript Governance, Member Identity Linkage, Intent Taxonomy) are foundation enablers, not bounded workflows, yet they are placed on an executive-priority-vs-readiness use-case matrix. This risks reading enablers as competing use-case candidates, blurring the foundation/use-case distinction the pack otherwise enforces well.
violations.remediation: Either restrict the matrix to the single workflow candidate with enablers shown as an annotation, or relabel the series/axis so enablers are visibly distinct from the qualified workflow.

violations.issue: module_implications is authored as an object with a headline and implications array here, while in the apps and rel dimensions it is an array of classified implication objects. The inconsistent shape, and the fact that the risks implications strings do not each carry a classification, weakens cross-dimension consistency.
violations.remediation: Align module_implications to the array-of-classified-objects shape used by the apps and rel dimensions, with each implication carrying a single classification.

violations.issue: The 'Evidence Confidence Across the Portfolio' horizontal_bar is classified derived_measure while its data_points are relative directional proxies (e.g., 90, 85, 35) explicitly described in the evidence_boundary as not measured probabilities. Labeling directional proxy scores as a derived_measure slightly overstates evidence posture.
violations.remediation: Reclassify the visual as strategic_inference to match its own evidence_boundary language, or provide the calculable basis that would justify derived_measure.
